english.title: Make explosive substance for unlawful purpose
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) made an explosive substance, namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE..), under such circumstances as to give rise to a reasonable suspicion that you were not making it for a lawful object
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1) of the Explosive Substances Act 1883.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

under circumstances giving reasonable suspicion
not making it for a lawful object

english.notes:
(i) H.M. Inspector of Explosives notes of guidance in the Guide state "The very wide powers and severe penalties contained in this Act are intended to be used only in serious cases....In cases of less importance, as for instance where a person damages property with an explosive to gratify personal spite, proceedings should be under the Malicious Injuries to property Act 1861 or Offences Against the Person Act 1861. Even where personal injury is caused maliciously by an explosive, the crime can be dealt with under the latter Act."
(ii) The consent of the Attorney General required.
(iii) See also offence wording: H1722.
(iv) From 13th April 2015, the maximum sentence was amended from 14 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. This amendment applies only in relation to an offence committed on or after 13th April 2015. Where an offence is found to have been committed over a period of 2 or more days, or at some time during a period of 2 or more days, it must be taken to have been committed on the last of those days.
(iv) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.
